item.title: Cleaning Crew 1099 vs W2 in 2026: The Real Compliance Math
item.description: Every cleaning business owner reaches the same fork in the road around client 10–15: hire help. And every one of them gets the same well-meaning advice from a friend, a Facebook group, or a random YouTube video: “Just 1099 them — it’s cheaper and easier.” That advice is technically legal in some cases, questionable in most, and financially catastrophic in the wrong case. The IRS + Department of Labor have spent the last decade tightening the definition of who legally qualifies as a 1099 independent contractor, and cleaning services is one of the categories they audit most aggressively.
